prompt_md: Roll two dice again and again. What's the chance you roll both a total of 6 and a total of 8 (in either order) before you ever roll a total of 7?
prompt_short: Two dice, repeated. Both a 6 and an 8 before any 7?
hint_md: Ignore every roll that isn't a 6, 7 or 8.
explain_intuition_md: A 6 beats a 7 with chance 5 in 11, and so does an 8, so multiplying gives about 21%. But the two races aren't independent: they're both against the same 7. First a 6 or an 8 must beat the 7, which is easier because either one will do; then the other number must beat the 7 too.
explain_math_md: Totals 6, 7, 8 come up in 5, 6, 5 ways out of 36: $$\tfrac{10}{16}\cdot\tfrac{5}{11} = \tfrac{25}{88} \approx 28.4\%$$
